title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Stocks fell again Wednesday (S&P 500 -0.5%, Dow -405 pts/-0.8%, Nasdaq -0.6%) after Tuesday's steeper 628-point Dow drop; September is living up to its weak seasonal reputation.

Markets: Oil surged further, Brent above $101/barrel and WTI near $97, after the U.S. struck Iranian oil tankers and Houthi forces hit Saudi Arabia; both benchmarks are up 60%+ year-to-date and U.S. diesel hit a record ~$5.90-5.94/gallon.

Markets: The 10-year Treasury yield jumped to about 4.85%, its highest in roughly three years, after the Treasury's new $6B long-bond buyback program (purchases begin today) came in smaller than investors had hoped.

Companies: Apple unveiled its first foldable iPhone ($1,999 starting price) under new CEO John Ternus and raised iPhone prices to offset rising memory/storage chip costs; shares dipped only 0.3%, outperforming the broader market.
Companies: Casey's General Stores plunged 14% on same-store sales growth that missed elevated expectations, while newly-IPO'd Jersey Mike's Subs rose 7.5% on its first earnings report.
Companies: An Anthropic AI safety researcher resigned, citing fears that AI labs are racing to build systems they won't be able to control, echoing departures at OpenAI and elsewhere.

Macro/Policy: Fed-hike odds for the Sept 15-16 FOMC meeting climbed to roughly 57-58% (from ~50%) as oil-driven inflation risk collides with a stronger-than-expected August jobs report (+162k vs. 65k consensus).
Macro/Policy: Thursday brings initial jobless claims, existing home sales, and producer price index data, plus earnings from Oracle and Adobe after the close.
